supersedes.reason: first successful BAS run showed tier 2 consuming 91.7 s of 100.6 s, 80% of it on resources that could not accept its output

classifier.architecture: MiniLM embedding + 256-unit ReLU hidden layer + 63-class softmax

relevance.behaviour: conservative: rejects most candidates, generation falls back to deterministic values and reports SFT_CANDIDATE_RELEVANCE_UNVERIFIED

pairedReplay.travel-v2 deterministic: rejected by design (no verifier in deterministic mode)

gateRevisions.relevancePositiveAcceptance: 0.80 floor -> non-degenerate, hard-negative budget kept at 1%

basFindings.reportedBy: package owner, first BAS linux-x64 run of 1.48.0
basFindings.workerEnvironment: client.ts allowedEnvironment() now forwards ASDF_*, npm_config_*, the proxy variables and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS; NODE_OPTIONS stays stripped
basFindings.onnxruntimeCudaDownload: runtime.ts installEnvironment() sets ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL=skip; onnxruntime-node 1.24.3 declares a cuda12 requirement for linux/x64 only, and MockGen runs the bundled CPU provider
basFindings.npmPublication: @unseen/mock-data-generator@0.1.0-dev.7 published by the package owner; download and integrity verification passed in BAS before the install step failed

tierGating.relevanceCircuit: once one resource has ended unverified - declined by the verifier, structurally invalid to the last attempt, or out of budget - the remaining resources reuse that outcome without calling the model; rows, diagnostics and coverage counters unchanged
tierGating.protocolArtifacts: entity sets in SAP Gateway's reserved SAP__ namespace are left to the deterministic tier, reported once as SFT_SKIPPED_PROTOCOL_ARTIFACTS

travelV2.options: mode auto, seed 123, 10 rows per entity, sftTimeoutMs 30000, sftBudgetMs 120000 (the editor worker defaults)
travelV2.note: same machine, same options; the before run was produced by disabling both gates in the built artifact

travelV2PairedReplay.options: mode auto, seed 123, 1 row per entity

selfReferenceFix.defect: the structural-property map created one set per relationship end, so a relationship whose source and target are the same entity set produced two sets for one key and the second write discarded the first, leaving one end's foreign key writable by the fine-tuned tier
selfReferenceFix.attribution: reproduces with both tier-2 gates disabled; invisible until now because the 2026-09-19 corpus baseline was recorded with sftBudgetMs 1, so tier 2 never ran
selfReferenceFix.beforeError: Generated relationship Genres.parent->Genres is not referentially valid (sourceRows=2, targetRows=2)

corpusBenchmark.note: same corpus, same code, three runs. The 2026-09-19 learned baseline is superseded because it used sftBudgetMs 1 without recording that, so tier 2 never ran in it; its numbers were medianMs 1516.5, p90Ms 3366.8, totalSec 269.3 (learned) and medianMs 96 (deterministic), measured against dev.7.

wholePipeline.settings: mode auto, 2 rows per entity, seed 123, packaged service budget

recognitionPath.settings: mode auto, 2 rows per entity, seed 123, sftBudgetMs 1 so tier 2 never fires

deterministic.settings: mode deterministic, 2 rows per entity, seed 123

valueTierAccounting.purpose: answer how much of a generated dataset each tier actually wrote, per value slot rather than per field
valueTierAccounting.buckets: declared and authored (T0), recognised (T1), model (T2), typed (T3), structural for foreign keys decided by relational assignment
valueTierAccounting.method: recorded at each value-producing return point, totalled from the published rows so later row expansion or key-domain reduction cannot make the total disagree with the dataset
valueTierAccounting.invariants: sum of the six buckets equals slots equals the published cell count; tiers.model equals statistics.sft.acceptedSlots; deterministic mode gives model 0
valueTierAccounting.logLine: [MockGen] Tiers: slots=, T0 declared=, T0 authored=, T1 recognised=, T2 model=, T3 typed=, structural=

travelV2.options: mode auto, seed 123, 10 rows per entity, editor worker budgets
